title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 1
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
The chart shows unit price and units sold for five product lines over one quarter.

Aster: unit price GBP 12.50, units sold 1,840
Briar: unit price GBP 9.75, units sold 2,310
Cedar: unit price GBP 18.20, units sold 1,120
Dovel: unit price GBP 7.40, units sold 3,050
Elmet: unit price GBP 15.60, units sold 1,360

Which product line generated the greatest revenue in the quarter?
options: A. Briar
B. Cedar
C. Aster
D. Dovel
E. Elmet
questions.explanation: Revenue is price multiplied by units, so the ranking cannot be read off either column alone. Aster GBP 23,000.00; Briar GBP 22,522.50; Cedar GBP 20,384.00; Dovel GBP 22,570.00; Elmet GBP 21,216.00. Aster is highest at GBP 23,000.00 — note that it has neither the highest price nor the highest volume.

questions.prompt:
Quarterly visitor numbers at a museum:

Q1: 41,200
Q2: 47,380
Q3: 52,118
Q4: 54,203

In which quarter was the percentage increase over the previous quarter greatest?
options: A. Q2
B. Q3
C. Q4
D. The increase was the same in each quarter
E. Cannot be determined without the prior year
questions.explanation: Percentage change, not absolute change: Q2 +15.0%, Q3 +10.0%, Q4 +4.0%. Q2 is largest. Q4 has a larger absolute rise than Q3 but a smaller percentage rise, which is the trap.

questions.prompt:
A pie chart shows the share of customer complaints by category:

Billing: 27%
Delivery: 22%
Product fault: 19%
Staff conduct: 14%
Website: 11%
Other: 7%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for more than half of all complaints?
options: A. Two
B. Three
C. Four
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Take the largest categories first: 27 + 22 = 49%, which does not exceed half. Adding Product fault gives 68%. So 3 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Waiting times recorded at seven branches on the same morning, in minutes:

4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 26, 31

Which statement about these figures is accurate?
options: A. The mean and the median are equal
B. The median is greater than the mean
C. The mean is more than twice the median
D. The mean is greater than the median
E. The mean cannot be determined from the data given
questions.explanation: Median is the fourth value, 9 minutes. Mean is 4+6+7+9+12+26+31 = 95 over 7, which is 13.57 minutes. The mean exceeds the median because two long waits pull it upward, but not by more than a factor of two.

questions.prompt:
Three electricity tariffs, each a fixed monthly charge plus a rate per unit:

Tariff A: fixed GBP 18.00, GBP 0.09 per unit
Tariff B: fixed GBP 26.00, GBP 0.06 per unit
Tariff C: fixed GBP 34.00, GBP 0.03 per unit

Select the tariff that is cheapest for a household using 200 units a month, AND the tariff that is cheapest for a household using 900 units a month.
options: A. Tariff A at 200 units; Tariff B at 900 units
B. Tariff A at 200 units; Tariff C at 900 units
C. Tariff B at 200 units; Tariff C at 900 units
D. Tariff C at 200 units; Tariff A at 900 units
E. The same tariff is cheapest at both levels
questions.explanation: At 200 units: Tariff A GBP 36.00, Tariff B GBP 37.00, Tariff C GBP 40.00. At 900 units: Tariff A GBP 99.00, Tariff B GBP 75.50, Tariff C GBP 61.00. The tariff with the lowest fixed charge wins at low usage and the one with the lowest rate wins at high usage.

questions.prompt:
Three suppliers quote for an order, each with a one-off setup charge and a price per unit:

Supplier P: setup GBP 1,200.00, GBP 3.10 per unit, lead time 12 days
Supplier Q: setup GBP 400.00, GBP 3.55 per unit, lead time 7 days
Supplier R: setup GBP 2,600.00, GBP 2.75 per unit, lead time 21 days

For an order of 5,000 units, select the supplier with the lowest total cost AND the supplier with the shortest lead time.
options: A. Lowest cost Supplier P; shortest lead time Supplier Q
B. Lowest cost Supplier P; shortest lead time Supplier R
C. Lowest cost Supplier Q; shortest lead time Supplier P
D. Lowest cost Supplier R; shortest lead time Supplier P
E. Lowest cost Supplier R; shortest lead time Supplier Q
questions.explanation: Total at 5,000 units: Supplier P GBP 16,700.00, Supplier Q GBP 18,150.00, Supplier R GBP 16,350.00. Supplier R is cheapest despite the highest setup charge, because the per-unit saving outweighs it at this volume. Lead times are given directly: Supplier Q is shortest at 7 days.

questions.prompt:
A firm's fixed costs are GBP 48,000.00 a year. Product X contributes GBP 12.00 per unit sold; Product Y contributes GBP 7.50 per unit.

Select the product that reaches break-even on fewer units AND the number of units at which it does so.
options: A. Product X; 4,000 units
B. Product X; 6,400 units
C. Product Y; 6,400 units
D. Product Y; 4,000 units
E. Both products break even at the same number of units
questions.explanation: Break-even units are fixed costs divided by contribution per unit: X needs 48000/12 = 4,000; Y needs 48000/7.5 = 6,400. The higher contribution reaches break-even sooner.

questions.prompt:
Two funds over the same period:

Fund A: opening value GBP 8,000.00, closing value GBP 11,600.00
Fund B: opening value GBP 12,000.00, closing value GBP 16,200.00

Select the fund with the larger gain in absolute terms AND the fund with the larger gain in percentage terms.
options: A. Fund A in absolute terms; Fund A in percentage terms
B. Fund A in absolute terms; Fund B in percentage terms
C. Fund B in absolute terms; Fund A in percentage terms
D. Fund B in absolute terms; Fund B in percentage terms
E. The two funds gained equally on both measures
questions.explanation: Absolute gains: Fund A GBP 3,600.00, Fund B GBP 4,200.00. Percentage gains: Fund A 45.0%, Fund B 35.0%. The larger fund gains more money and the smaller fund gains more proportionally, which is why the two measures disagree.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo from the operations director): "Service quality has improved every month this quarter."

SOURCE 2 (table of complaints received):
January: 480
February: 505
March: 560

SOURCE 3 (email from the sales team): "Order volumes were January 40,000, February 55,000, March 80,000."

Which statement is best supported by the three sources together?
options: A. The memo is contradicted, because complaints rose each month
B. The memo is confirmed, because complaints per order fell to zero
C. The sources are consistent only if the table is inaccurate
D. Complaints rose in total while complaints per thousand orders fell
E. No conclusion about complaint rates can be drawn without knowing the value of each order
questions.explanation: Totals rise (480 to 505 to 560), but per thousand orders the rate is January 12.00, February 9.18, March 7.00. Source 2 alone supports the first option and Source 3 alone supports none; only the two together settle it, which is the point of the format.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "The new shelf layout raised sales in our trial stores by 15% year on year, so we should adopt it everywhere."

SOURCE 2 (table, year-on-year sales change): Trial stores +15.2%; all other stores +14.1%; company overall +14.3%.

SOURCE 3 (email from the regional manager): "The trial stores also received two extra staff each for the trial period."

Which of the following is best supported?
options: A. The layout raised sales by about 15 percentage points
B. The layout had no effect on sales in any store
C. Sales fell in stores that did not receive the new layout
D. The trial cannot be evaluated because sales figures are unreliable
E. The layout's effect is at most about one percentage point, and part of even that may be due to the extra staff
questions.explanation: The memo compares the trial stores with their own past. Against the correct comparison — other stores over the same period — the difference is 15.2 minus 14.1, about one percentage point, and Source 3 supplies a second change that could account for some of it. Option B overstates in the other direction: the data do not establish an effect of exactly zero.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (quality report): "Defect rates by supplier: Supplier S1 0.8%, Supplier S2 2.1%, Supplier S3 1.4%."

SOURCE 2 (purchasing table, units supplied this year): Supplier S1 120,000, Supplier S2 45,000, Supplier S3 70,000

SOURCE 3 (email): "We should concentrate improvement work where it will remove the largest number of defective units."

On which supplier should the improvement work concentrate?
options: A. Supplier S1
B. Supplier S3
C. Supplier S2
D. The three suppliers contribute equally
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Defective units are volume multiplied by rate: Supplier S1 960, Supplier S2 945, Supplier S3 980. The supplier with the highest defect rate is not the one producing the most defective units, and the one with the largest volume is not either.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Regional revenue grew 9% in Region A and 12% in Region B, both measured in local currency."

SOURCE 2 (finance note): "Region B's local currency weakened by 10% against the reporting currency over the year; Region A's was unchanged."

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board reviews growth in the reporting currency."

Which statement is best supported for the measure the board reviews?
options: A. Region A grew faster than Region B
B. Region B grew faster than Region A
C. The two regions grew at the same rate
D. Region B's revenue in the reporting currency grew by 12%
E. Neither region's growth can be expressed in the reporting currency
questions.explanation: In the reporting currency Region B's 12% local growth is reduced by the 10% currency fall: 1.12 multiplied by 0.90 is 1.008, about 0.8% growth. Region A is unaffected at 9%. The ranking reverses once the sources are combined, which is why Source 1 alone is misleading.

questions.prompt:
A shop sold 240 items in a day, each priced at either GBP 15.00 or GBP 22.00. What was the shop's total takings from these items?

(1) 90 of the items were priced at GBP 15.00.
(2) Takings from the items priced at GBP 22.00 were GBP 3,300.00.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), 90 at 15 and 150 at 22 gives 1,350 + 3,300 = 4,650 — sufficient. From (2), 3,300/22 = 150 items at 22, leaving 90 at 15, giving the same 4,650 — also sufficient. Each statement alone determines the total, so the answer is D rather than C.

questions.prompt:
Is the integer x greater than 12?

(1) 3x > 30
(2) x is a multiple of 4 and x > 8
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives x > 10, so x could be 11 or 20 — insufficient. (2) allows 12, 16, 20 — and 12 is not greater than 12, so insufficient. Together, x > 10 and a multiple of 4 above 8 still allows 12 (answer no) and 16 (answer yes). Not sufficient even combined.

questions.prompt:
What were a branch's mean weekly sales over a four-week period?

(1) Total sales for the four weeks were GBP 18,400.00.
(2) Sales in the first three weeks averaged GBP 4,500.00 a week.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The mean is the total divided by four, so (1) gives 18,400/4 = 4,600 — sufficient. (2) fixes only the first three weeks and says nothing about the fourth, so the four-week mean could be almost anything — insufficient.

questions.prompt:
Did a club's membership increase from 2024 to 2025?

(1) Membership in 2025 was 12% higher than in 2023.
(2) Membership in 2024 was 20% higher than in 2023.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Neither statement alone relates 2024 to 2025. Together, 2025 is 1.12 times the 2023 figure and 2024 is 1.20 times it, so 2025 is 1.12/1.20 = 0.93 times 2024 — a decrease. The question is answered definitively, and a definite "no" is sufficiency.

questions.prompt:
Which warehouse shipped the most orders per member of staff?

Warehouse | Orders shipped | Error rate | Staff
Alder | 12,400 | 1.8% | 34
Byfield | 13,000 | 0.9% | 22
Corfe | 15,800 | 2.4% | 41
Denby | 7,600 | 1.1% | 18
Eaton | 18,250 | 1.6% | 47
Frome | 11,050 | 3.2% | 26
options: A. Alder
B. Corfe
C. Byfield
D. Denby
E. Eaton
questions.explanation: Orders divided by staff: Alder 364.7, Byfield 590.9, Corfe 385.4, Denby 422.2, Eaton 388.3, Frome 425.0. Byfield is highest. The warehouse shipping the most orders in total is not the most productive per head.

questions.prompt:
How many warehouses have an error rate above the median error rate for the six?

Warehouse | Orders shipped | Error rate | Staff
Alder | 12,400 | 1.8% | 34
Byfield | 13,000 | 0.9% | 22
Corfe | 15,800 | 2.4% | 41
Denby | 7,600 | 1.1% | 18
Eaton | 18,250 | 1.6% | 47
Frome | 11,050 | 3.2% | 26
options: A. One
B. Three
C. Two
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: With six values the median is the average of the third and fourth: (1.6 + 1.8)/2 = 1.7%. Rates above 1.7% are Alder 1.8%, Corfe 2.4%, Frome 3.2% — 3 warehouses.

questions.prompt:
Which warehouse shipped the greatest number of orders containing errors?

Warehouse | Orders shipped | Error rate | Staff
Alder | 12,400 | 1.8% | 34
Byfield | 13,000 | 0.9% | 22
Corfe | 15,800 | 2.4% | 41
Denby | 7,600 | 1.1% | 18
Eaton | 18,250 | 1.6% | 47
Frome | 11,050 | 3.2% | 26
options: A. Alder
B. Byfield
C. Denby
D. Corfe
E. Eaton
questions.explanation: Erroneous orders are orders multiplied by the error rate: Alder 223, Byfield 117, Corfe 379, Denby 84, Eaton 292, Frome 354. Corfe is highest at about 379. Frome has the worst rate but ships too few orders to top the count.

questions.prompt:
Rank the warehouses by orders shipped (highest first) and separately by error rate (lowest first). Which warehouse's two ranks differ by the largest amount?

Warehouse | Orders shipped | Error rate | Staff
Alder | 12,400 | 1.8% | 34
Byfield | 13,000 | 0.9% | 22
Corfe | 15,800 | 2.4% | 41
Denby | 7,600 | 1.1% | 18
Eaton | 18,250 | 1.6% | 47
Frome | 11,050 | 3.2% | 26
options: A. Alder
B. Byfield
C. Corfe
D. Eaton
E. Denby
questions.explanation: By orders: Eaton, Corfe, Byfield, Alder, Frome, Denby. By error rate, best first: Byfield, Denby, Eaton, Alder, Corfe, Frome. Rank differences: Alder 0, Byfield 2, Corfe 3, Denby 4, Eaton 2, Frome 1. Denby differs by 4 — it is nearly last for volume and near the top for accuracy.
